title: Verdier Hom bijections for chosen structure adjoints on geometric Weil pairs
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $k$ an algebraic closure, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ a prime, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $T_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$. Write $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,\Omega)$ for the common-stage coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ for geometric-Frobenius pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $\mathrm W(T_0)=\mathcal C_T^{P_T}$ be the category of pairs $(K,\theta:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ and commuting morphisms [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. All categories in this assertion are these fixed-pair categories. Use compact support and its canonical lifted constructible exceptional adjunction [cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance]. Let $a_0:T_0\to s_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be the structure map, choose any adjunction $Ra_{0!}\dashv J_T$ on these pair categories, and put $\omega_T=J_T\Omega_{s_0}$, where $\Omega_{s_0}$ is the coefficient unit with canonical Frobenius structure. Use internal Hom with its standard Weil lift [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $J_T^{\rm can}$ denote the canonical lifted structure right adjoint, $\omega_T^{\rm can}=J_T^{\rm can}\Omega_{s_0}$, and $D_T^{\rm can}=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T^{\rm can})$.

The counit-compatible right-adjoint comparison $J_T\xrightarrow{\sim}J_T^{\rm can}$ induces a Weil isomorphism $n_T:\omega_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_T^{\rm can}$. The functor $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$ preserves $\mathrm W(T_0)$ and postcomposition with $n_T$ gives a natural Weil isomorphism $D_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_T^{\rm can}$. The specified functor $D_T$ is an anti-equivalence, has natural Weil biduality $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_TD_TK$, and its action on arrows gives bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm W(T_0)}(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm W(T_0)}(D_TB,D_TA),\qquad u\longmapsto D_T(u),$$
natural in $A,B$.

proof.text: Obtain B, IH, W and DualizingNormalization from cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance. For each compactification choose its recorded A and Z from the normalization. Apply the existing closed fixed-pair adjunction construction lem-sf-fixed-pair-adjunction-lift to A.adjunction, Z.common.left and its mate Z.common.right. Its carrier unit and counit are definitionally those of A.adjunction. Unpack the common DualizingMate to obtain the normalized coefficient-unit structure and the equivariant isomorphism iω from the geometric dualizing pair to the canonical right adjoint applied to that unit. Apply det-sp-unique-right-adjoint to any chosen adjunction to set n to the specified component of rightAdjointUniq.

source.place: Paragraphs 1–2: lifted exceptional adjunction and equivariant biduality; formal normalization by uniqueness of right adjoints

proof.text: For each common-stage pair, B.finite.hom at its compositum already supplies the permitted internal-Hom domain. Internal-Hom bifunctoriality gives the natural isomorphism H(-,omega) → H(-,omega′) induced by a target isomorphism n, with precisely component H(identity,n). Compose the canonical target comparison for iω inverse with IH.comparison inverse to obtain the underlying comparison to geometricDual. Lift the literal Hom functor by conjugating the geometric Weil structure through this comparison: theta_H = e composed with the old structure and inverse e (with the Frobenius functor applied to the first factor). Naturality of e and the old Weil-arrow equation prove the new arrow equation. This leaves its carrier objects and carrier maps definitionally the specified Hom operation. The same construction using the component n of rightAdjointUniq produces the chosen Hom functor and its comparison to the canonical Hom functor.

source.place: Displayed dual Weil structure and paragraph 2: natural internal-Hom comparison; explicit substitution of the dualizing-object isomorphism

proof.text: Lift the isomorphism B.duality.bidual componentwise to fixed pairs using W.common.biduality_equivariant; naturality follows from the underlying biduality naturality and faithful carrier morphisms. Transport this natural biduality first along the canonical Hom comparison and then along the chosen Hom comparison. Explicitly c:V≅C gives the opposite component isomorphism C.rightOp≅V.rightOp; whisker it by C and then whisker c inverse by V.rightOp. Compose these with the old biduality. The opposite of the new biduality gives the second inverse identity, so Functor.IsEquivalence.mk′ proves that V is an anti-equivalence.

source.place: Paragraph 2: equivariant biduality, transported through the natural isomorphism constructed in Step 2

proof.text: Use the fully faithful Hom bijection of V, composed with the elementary equivalence from arrows K→M to arrows op M→op K. The composite forward map is definitionally f↦V.map f.op, so it is the requested actual dual arrow action. Finally op_comp and Functor.map_comp give the both-variable naturality equation.
